To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) ML type systems are not only a means of identifying well behaved programs but also of providing convenient shorthand for programs in typed calculi; (2) ML type systems can be used as a basis for the development of new type systems; (3) ML type systems provide a convenient basis for the study of the semantics of ML programs, including the study of ML polymorphism; (4) ML type systems have been used as a basis of a number of practical programming languages.
ML type checking is a form of implicit type inference, and that ML type checking and implicit polymorphic type inference are two sides of the same coin.

the ML type system can be viewed as a type system for a language that has qualified types and explicit polymorphic type variables, that the ML type inference algorithm can be viewed as an algorithm for inferring qualified type annotations, that the ML polymorphic type inference algorithm can similarly be viewed as an inference algorithm for qualified type annotations, and that the ML polymorphism is a special case of qualified type polymorphism, in which qualified types are not explicitly represented.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation and application of typed languages.
the relationship between core-ML programs and programs in other languages.
the design, implementation, and application of type systems for ML-style languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ML is a type system for core-ML, which is a convenient shorthand for a typed language.
ML type systems are useful for the analysis and specification of a wide range of programming languages.
ML type systems have been studied in depth, and that the resulting theory is well understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ML type system is a convenient shorthand for a wide range of typed languages.

we have developed a theory of type systems for ML that can be used to reason about the behaviour of programs in typed languages, and which can be used to develop tools for type checking and type inference.
ML polymorphism is not a good fit for the ML type system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
core-ML programs are a convenient way of expressing programs in typed languages, but that they should not be confused with typed programs.
ML polymorphism is not as straightforward as it may appear at first.
core-ML can be viewed as a convenient shorthand for programs written in a typed language, and that core-ML programs can be translated into typed languages.
